title: The Four Purposes of Preaching Los Cuatro Propósitos de la Predicación

blocks.en: Unit Ten · The Purposes of Preaching
blocks.es_reference: Unidad Diez · Los Propósitos de la Predicación

blocks.en: The Four Purposes of Preaching
blocks.es_reference: Los Cuatro Propósitos de la Predicación

blocks.en: You have learned a method. The same sermon, built the same way, may be preached toward very different ends. What changes from one sermon to the next is not the craft in your hands but the purpose in your heart. Across the centuries the Christian pulpit has served four great purposes — to teach, to convert, to heal, and to confront.
blocks.es_reference: Usted ha aprendido un método. El mismo sermón, construido de la misma manera, puede predicarse con fines muy distintos. Lo que cambia de un sermón a otro no es el arte en sus manos sino el propósito en su corazón. A lo largo de los siglos el púlpito cristiano ha servido a cuatro grandes propósitos — enseñar, convertir, sanar y confrontar.

blocks.en: 10.1 Purpose and Structure
blocks.es_reference: 10.1 Propósito y Estructura

blocks.en: A method is a tool, and a tool can be turned to more than one task. The Apostle Paul gathered the purposes of preaching when he charged Timothy to "preach the word" and to do it "in season, out of season," to "reprove, rebuke, exhort, with all longsuffering and teaching" (2 Timothy 4:2). In that one verse the sermon both comforts and confronts; it teaches and it pleads. The faithful preacher learns to recognize which purpose a given congregation, text, and hour requires, and to bend his method toward it.
blocks.es_reference: Un método es una herramienta, y una herramienta puede emplearse para más de una tarea. El apóstol Pablo reunió los propósitos de la predicación cuando encargó a Timoteo: "predica la palabra; insta a tiempo y fuera de tiempo; redarguye, reprende, exhorta con toda paciencia y enseñanza" (2 Timoteo 4:2). En ese solo versículo el sermón consuela y confronta; enseña y suplica. El predicador fiel aprende a reconocer cuál propósito requieren una congregación, un texto y una hora determinados, y a inclinar su método hacia él.

blocks.en: These four purposes are a matter of the sermon's aim, not its shape. How a sermon is built — topical, textual, expository, or narrative — is a separate question of structure, and structure has little to do with how biblical a sermon is. Every sermon must be biblical; not every sermon is expository. Here our concern is purpose: why we preach a given message, and what we mean it to accomplish. We will take each of the four in turn.
blocks.es_reference: Estos cuatro propósitos son cuestión del fin del sermón, no de su forma. Cómo se construye un sermón — temático, textual, expositivo o narrativo — es una cuestión aparte de estructura, y la estructura tiene poco que ver con cuán bíblico es un sermón. Todo sermón debe ser bíblico; no todo sermón es expositivo. Aquí nuestra atención está en el propósito: por qué predicamos un mensaje dado, y qué pretendemos lograr con él. Tomaremos cada uno de los cuatro por turno.

blocks.en: 10.2 Doctrinal Preaching — To Teach
blocks.es_reference: 10.2 Predicación Doctrinal — Enseñar

blocks.en: The doctrinal sermon takes a basic Christian belief — the cross, the new birth, justification by faith, the Person of Christ, the resurrection, the last things — and preaches it with a view to gaining understanding and acceptance. Its purpose is not merely to inform the mind but to win the heart's consent and then to govern the life. A great doctrine is laid open, explained in plain words, defended where the hearer's questions or the errors of the age require it, and pressed home until the listener not only grasps the truth but lives by it.
blocks.es_reference: El sermón doctrinal toma una creencia cristiana fundamental — la cruz, el nuevo nacimiento, la justificación por la fe, la Persona de Cristo, la resurrección, las últimas cosas — y la predica con miras a la comprensión y la aceptación. Su propósito no es solo informar la mente, sino ganar el consentimiento del corazón y luego gobernar la vida. Una gran doctrina se expone, se explica con palabras sencillas, se defiende donde lo exigen las preguntas del oyente o los errores de la época, y se aplica hasta que el oyente no solo capta la verdad sino que vive conforme a ella.

blocks.en: In its structure, doctrinal preaching is usually topical preaching. A great doctrine is rarely confined to a single passage; it is gathered from throughout the Bible — the new birth from John, Romans, and Peter; the atonement from Isaiah, the Gospels, and Hebrews. So the doctrinal sermon collects its truth from many texts and arranges it around one theme, which is exactly what a topical sermon does. This makes it no less biblical than an expository message. Topical, textual, and expository describe how a sermon is arranged, not how faithful it is to Scripture; every sermon must be biblical, but not every sermon need be expository.
blocks.es_reference: En su estructura, la predicación doctrinal suele ser predicación temática. Una gran doctrina rara vez se limita a un solo pasaje; se reúne de toda la Biblia — el nuevo nacimiento de Juan, Romanos y Pedro; la expiación de Isaías, los Evangelios y Hebreos. Así el sermón doctrinal recoge su verdad de muchos textos y la organiza en torno a un tema, que es justo lo que hace un sermón temático. Esto no lo hace menos bíblico que un mensaje expositivo. Temático, textual y expositivo describen cómo se ordena un sermón, no cuán fiel es a la Escritura; todo sermón debe ser bíblico, pero no todo sermón necesita ser expositivo.

blocks.en: The doctrinal preacher must remember that he is preaching, not lecturing. The constant danger of this kind of sermon is that it hardens into a classroom lesson, as dry as Ezekiel's bones, full of explanation and empty of life. The cure is to keep three things together: make the doctrine clear (take one truth, not ten, and let the whole sermon serve it); make it warm (a doctrine is a window onto the character of God, and should leave the hearer worshiping); and make it applied (every doctrine carries a "therefore" — if Christ is risen, then do not fear the grave). Paul charged Titus to "speak the things which befit the sound doctrine" (Titus 2:1). It is the backbone of a healthy pulpit, and every other purpose depends on it.
blocks.es_reference: El predicador doctrinal debe recordar que está predicando, no dictando una conferencia. El peligro constante de esta clase de sermón es que se endurezca en una lección de aula, tan seca como los huesos de Ezequiel, llena de explicación y vacía de vida. El remedio es mantener juntas tres cosas: hacer la doctrina clara (tome una sola verdad, no diez, y que todo el sermón le sirva); hacerla cálida (una doctrina es una ventana al carácter de Dios, y debe dejar al oyente adorando); y hacerla aplicada (toda doctrina lleva un "por tanto" — si Cristo ha resucitado, no tema la tumba). Pablo encargó a Tito: "habla lo que está de acuerdo con la sana doctrina" (Tito 2:1). Es la columna vertebral de un púlpito sano, y todo otro propósito depende de ella.

blocks.en: 10.3 Evangelistic Preaching — To Convert
blocks.es_reference: 10.3 Predicación Evangelística — Convertir

blocks.en: The evangelistic sermon proclaims the gospel of Jesus Christ and calls the hearer to a decision. Where the doctrinal sermon labors chiefly for understanding, the evangelistic sermon labors for response. It sets the dark truth of sin against the bright truth of grace, lifts up Christ crucified and risen as the only Savior, and presses the listener to receive him — not someday, but today.
blocks.es_reference: El sermón evangelístico proclama el evangelio de Jesucristo y llama al oyente a una decisión. Donde el sermón doctrinal trabaja sobre todo por la comprensión, el evangelístico trabaja por la respuesta. Contrapone la oscura verdad del pecado con la luminosa verdad de la gracia, levanta a Cristo crucificado y resucitado como el único Salvador, e insta al oyente a recibirlo — no algún día, sino hoy.

blocks.en: Urgency is the mark of this preaching. Paul wrote, "now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation" (2 Corinthians 6:2). The evangelistic preacher believes that every time the gospel is heard a decision is being made, and that there is no neutral ground. He warms the heart, he reasons with the will, and he does not leave the sermon without a clear and earnest invitation; the whole message rises toward that appeal as toward its summit. Felix trembled under Paul's reasoning of righteousness, temperance, and judgment, yet put off his decision to a more convenient season that never came (Acts 24:25). The evangelist preaches so that his hearers will not make that fatal delay. Every other kind of sermon may borrow this urgency; a doctrinal or pastoral message that ends with a clear call to Christ is the stronger for it.
blocks.es_reference: La urgencia es la marca de esta predicación. Pablo escribió: "he aquí ahora el tiempo aceptable; he aquí ahora el día de salvación" (2 Corintios 6:2). El predicador evangelístico cree que cada vez que se oye el evangelio se toma una decisión, y que no hay terreno neutral. Enciende el corazón, razona con la voluntad, y no deja el sermón sin una invitación clara y ferviente; todo el mensaje asciende hacia ese llamado como hacia su cumbre. Félix tembló bajo el razonamiento de Pablo sobre la justicia, el dominio propio y el juicio, y sin embargo postergó su decisión para una ocasión más conveniente que nunca llegó (Hechos 24:25). El evangelista predica para que sus oyentes no cometan esa demora fatal. Todo otro tipo de sermón puede tomar prestada esta urgencia; un mensaje doctrinal o pastoral que termina con un claro llamado a Cristo es más fuerte por ello.

blocks.en: 10.4 Therapeutic (Pastoral) Preaching — To Heal
blocks.es_reference: 10.4 Predicación Terapéutica (Pastoral) — Sanar

blocks.en: This sermon is called by several names — pastoral preaching, therapeutic preaching, or life-situation preaching — but they all describe the same thing: a sermon that meets people where they hurt and brings the comfort and counsel of God's Word to bear upon a real human need. Where doctrinal preaching begins with a truth and evangelistic preaching with the gospel call, pastoral preaching often begins with a problem — grief, fear, guilt, loneliness, a marriage under strain, a wound that will not close — and then brings Scripture to that need as balm and as guide.
blocks.es_reference: Este sermón recibe varios nombres — predicación pastoral, predicación terapéutica o predicación de situación de vida — pero todos describen lo mismo: un sermón que encuentra a las personas donde sufren y aplica el consuelo y el consejo de la Palabra de Dios a una necesidad humana real. Donde la predicación doctrinal comienza con una verdad y la evangelística con el llamado del evangelio, la predicación pastoral a menudo comienza con un problema — duelo, temor, culpa, soledad, un matrimonio en tensión, una herida que no cierra — y luego lleva la Escritura a esa necesidad como bálsamo y como guía.

blocks.en: The warrant for this preaching is the shepherd's heart of God himself, who "healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds" (Psalm 147:3), and of the Lord Jesus, who said, "Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Matthew 11:28). Paul wrote to a grieving church not with platitudes but with the hope of the resurrection, "that ye sorrow not, even as the rest, who have no hope" (1 Thessalonians 4:13). To approach it well, begin with the real situation your people face, name it honestly, and then let the Scripture speak to it — not the other way around. But here is its peril, and it is a serious one: pastoral preaching must never decay into mere self-help or borrowed pop-psychology — comfort without Christ, advice without authority. The world has counsel enough; the people of God need a word from God. Let the sermon meet the need, but let it heal with Scripture and not merely soothe with sentiment.
blocks.es_reference: El fundamento de esta predicación es el corazón de pastor de Dios mismo, que "sana a los quebrantados de corazón, y venda sus heridas" (Salmo 147:3), y del Señor Jesús, que dijo: "Venid a mí todos los que estáis trabajados y cargados, y yo os haré descansar" (Mateo 11:28). Pablo escribió a una iglesia que lloraba, no con frases huecas, sino con la esperanza de la resurrección, "para que no os entristezcáis como los demás que no tienen esperanza" (1 Tesalonicenses 4:13). Para abordarla bien, comience con la situación real que enfrenta su gente, nómbrela con honestidad, y luego deje que la Escritura le hable — no al revés. Pero aquí está su peligro, y es serio: la predicación pastoral nunca debe degenerar en mera autoayuda o psicología popular prestada — consuelo sin Cristo, consejo sin autoridad. El mundo tiene consejo de sobra; el pueblo de Dios necesita una palabra de Dios. Que el sermón atienda la necesidad, pero que sane con la Escritura y no solo calme con sentimiento.

blocks.en: 10.5 Ethical (Prophetic) Preaching — To Confront
blocks.es_reference: 10.5 Predicación Ética (Profética) — Confrontar

blocks.en: The ethical sermon — often called prophetic preaching — calls the people of God to righteous living and lays the claims of God's holiness upon their conduct, both personal and public. Where pastoral preaching binds up wounds, ethical preaching probes them; where the one comforts, the other confronts. It names sin plainly, summons the hearer to repentance, and marks out the road of obedience. This is the preaching of the prophets: what does the LORD require of you, asked Micah, but "to do justly, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with thy God" (Micah 6:8)? It is the preaching of John the Baptist, who told the crowds to "bring forth fruit worthy of repentance" (Matthew 3:8). Above all it is pictured in Nathan, who went to a king guilty of adultery and murder and, by a story that disarmed him, brought him at last to the words "Thou art the man" (2 Samuel 12:7).
blocks.es_reference: El sermón ético — a menudo llamado predicación profética — llama al pueblo de Dios a una vida justa y pone las demandas de la santidad de Dios sobre su conducta, tanto personal como pública. Donde la predicación pastoral venda heridas, la ética las examina; donde una consuela, la otra confronta. Nombra el pecado con claridad, convoca al oyente al arrepentimiento, y traza el camino de la obediencia. Esta es la predicación de los profetas: ¿qué pide Jehová de ti, preguntó Miqueas, sino "hacer justicia, y amar misericordia, y humillarte ante tu Dios" (Miqueas 6:8)? Es la predicación de Juan el Bautista, que dijo a las multitudes: "haced frutos dignos de arrepentimiento" (Mateo 3:8). Sobre todo se retrata en Natán, que fue a un rey culpable de adulterio y homicidio y, con una historia que lo desarmó, lo llevó al fin a las palabras "Tú eres aquel hombre" (2 Samuel 12:7).

blocks.en: Yet ethical preaching has its own danger. It can curdle into mere moralism — a list of duties cut off from the gospel — or into bare social commentary that scolds without saving. The remedy is to root every command in grace. We do not preach righteousness as the way to earn God's favor, but as the glad response of those who have already received it. Law tells us what to do; only the gospel gives us the heart to do it. The ethical sermon presses obedience, but always upon a people first reminded of the mercy that makes obedience possible.
blocks.es_reference: Sin embargo, la predicación ética tiene su propio peligro. Puede cuajarse en mero moralismo — una lista de deberes separada del evangelio — o en simple comentario social que regaña sin salvar. El remedio es arraigar todo mandamiento en la gracia. No predicamos la justicia como el modo de ganar el favor de Dios, sino como la respuesta gozosa de quienes ya lo han recibido. La ley nos dice qué hacer; solo el evangelio nos da el corazón para hacerlo. El sermón ético insta a la obediencia, pero siempre sobre un pueblo al que primero se le ha recordado la misericordia que hace posible la obediencia.

blocks.en: 10.6 One Method, Many Aims
blocks.es_reference: 10.6 Un Método, Muchos Fines

blocks.en: Doctrinal, evangelistic, therapeutic, ethical — to teach, to convert, to heal, to confront. A single sermon will often serve more than one of them at once: a doctrinal message may close with an evangelistic appeal; a pastoral word may carry an ethical edge. The wise preacher knows which purpose his text and his people require, and he bends his craft toward it. The WiseSpeak method you have learned equips you for all four. The skill is the same; what you bring to it is the purpose. Learn to ask, before each sermon, not only "What does this text say?" but "What is this sermon for?"
blocks.es_reference: Doctrinal, evangelística, terapéutica, ética — enseñar, convertir, sanar, confrontar. Un solo sermón a menudo servirá a más de uno de ellos a la vez: un mensaje doctrinal puede cerrar con un llamado evangelístico; una palabra pastoral puede llevar un filo ético. El predicador sabio sabe cuál propósito requieren su texto y su gente, e inclina su arte hacia él. El método de HablaSabia que ha aprendido le capacita para los cuatro. La destreza es la misma; lo que usted aporta es el propósito. Aprenda a preguntar, antes de cada sermón, no solo "¿Qué dice este texto?" sino "¿Para qué es este sermón?"

mc.stem: This unit identifies four great purposes of preaching. They are:
mc.why: The four purposes (aims) are doctrinal — to teach, evangelistic — to convert, therapeutic/pastoral — to heal, and ethical/prophetic — to confront. The first option lists structures, not purposes.

mc.stem: The chief aim of doctrinal preaching is to —
options: call for an immediate decision for Christ
comfort the grieving and the fearful
help hearers understand and accept a Christian belief and live by it
mc.why: Doctrinal preaching teaches a belief with a view to understanding, acceptance, and a changed life.

mc.stem: In its structure, doctrinal preaching is usually —
options: expository preaching of a single passage
topical preaching, because a doctrine is gathered from throughout the Bible
mc.why: A doctrine is rarely confined to one text; it is gathered from across Scripture, so the doctrinal sermon is topical in structure.

mc.stem: Topical, textual, and expository are categories that describe a sermon's —
options: structure, not its faithfulness to Scripture
mc.why: These describe how a sermon is arranged. A topical sermon is no less biblical than an expository one.

mc.stem: Which statement reflects the unit's teaching on form and Scripture?
options: Only expository sermons are truly biblical
Every sermon must be biblical, but not every sermon need be expository
Doctrinal preaching is less biblical than expository
mc.why: Faithfulness to Scripture is required of every sermon; the expository structure is one good option among several, not the test of biblicalness.

mc.stem: The characteristic danger of doctrinal preaching is that it can —
options: become a dry classroom lecture, full of explanation and empty of life
mc.why: Doctrine must be preached, not merely lectured — kept clear, warm, and applied.

mc.stem: Evangelistic preaching labors chiefly for —
options: a decision — the hearer's response to receive Christ
mc.why: Where doctrinal preaching works for understanding, evangelistic preaching works for response.

mc.stem: Evangelistic preaching characteristically rises toward —
options: a clear and earnest invitation to respond now
mc.why: The whole message moves toward the appeal as toward its summit.

mc.stem: Which Scripture expresses the urgency of evangelistic preaching?
options: 'Be still, and know that I am God' (Psalm 46:10)
'Now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation' (2 Corinthians 6:2)
'In my Father's house are many mansions' (John 14:2)
mc.why: 2 Corinthians 6:2 — the evangelist presses for a decision today, not someday.

mc.stem: The account of Felix, who put off his decision to 'a more convenient season,' warns against —
options: the fatal delay of a postponed decision
mc.why: Felix trembled but delayed; the convenient season never came (Acts 24:25).

mc.stem: Therapeutic (pastoral) preaching aims above all to —
options: heal — meeting people in their hurts and needs with God's comfort
mc.why: Pastoral preaching brings the comfort and counsel of God's Word to a real human need.

mc.stem: Which set of terms all name the same kind of preaching?
mc.why: Pastoral, therapeutic, and life-situation preaching all describe the sermon that meets people where they hurt.

mc.stem: Which Scripture grounds pastoral preaching's ministry of comfort?
options: 'He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds' (Psalm 147:3)
'Now is the day of salvation' (2 Corinthians 6:2)
mc.why: Psalm 147:3 and Matthew 11:28 reveal the shepherd-heart of God that pastoral preaching reflects.

mc.stem: The serious peril of pastoral preaching is that it can decay into —
options: mere self-help or pop-psychology — comfort without Christ
mc.why: The world has counsel enough; the people of God need a word from God. It must heal with Scripture, not merely soothe with sentiment.

mc.stem: To approach pastoral preaching well, the preacher should —
options: begin with a doctrine and never mention the problem
begin with the real situation his people face, then bring Scripture to it
preach only on the end times
mc.why: Name the need honestly, then let the Scripture speak to it — not the other way around.

mc.stem: Ethical (prophetic) preaching chiefly —
options: calls God's people to righteous living and names sin
mc.why: Where pastoral preaching binds up wounds, ethical preaching probes them and calls to repentance and obedience.

mc.stem: Nathan's words to King David, 'Thou art the man' (2 Samuel 12:7), illustrate —
options: prophetic confrontation of sin, even with the powerful
mc.why: Nathan confronted a king guilty of adultery and murder; the prophetic preacher must be faithful even when unwelcome.

mc.stem: Which pairing belongs to ethical (prophetic) preaching?
options: 'Come unto me, all ye that labor' / 'I will give you rest'
'Do justly, love mercy, walk humbly' (Micah 6:8) / 'Bring forth fruit worthy of repentance' (Matthew 3:8)
mc.why: Micah and John the Baptist measured life against God's righteousness and called for repentance.

mc.stem: Ethical preaching guards against moralism by —
options: removing all commands from the sermon
rooting every command in grace, not presenting righteousness as a way to earn God's favor
mc.why: Law tells us what to do; only the gospel gives the heart to do it. Obedience is the glad response of those who have already received mercy.

mc.stem: According to the unit, a single sermon —
options: can serve only one of the four purposes
may serve more than one purpose at once (e.g., a doctrinal message closing with an evangelistic appeal)
has no purpose, only a structure
mc.why: The purposes often overlap; the wise preacher knows which purpose his text and people require and bends his craft toward it.

sa.prompt: Name the four purposes of preaching taught in this unit, and in a phrase state what each one aims to accomplish.
sa.model: Strong answer names all four and their aims: doctrinal — to teach a Christian belief for understanding and acceptance; evangelistic — to convert, calling the hearer to a decision for Christ; therapeutic/pastoral — to heal, meeting people's hurts and needs with God's comfort; ethical/prophetic — to confront sin and call God's people to righteous living. Weak answer names fewer than four, or confuses purposes with structures (topical/expository).

sa.prompt: Explain why doctrinal preaching is usually topical in structure, and defend the claim that it is no less biblical than expository preaching.
sa.model: Strong answer explains that a doctrine (the new birth, the atonement, justification) is rarely found in a single passage but is gathered from throughout the Bible, so the doctrinal sermon collects its truth from many texts and arranges it around one theme — which is exactly what a topical sermon does. It then argues that topical, textual, and expository describe how a sermon is structured, not how faithful it is to Scripture: every sermon must be biblical, but not every sermon need be expository. A doctrinal/topical sermon rightly drawn from many texts is fully biblical.

sa.prompt: Distinguish a sermon's purpose from its structure. Give one example of a single purpose being carried by a particular structure.
sa.model: Purpose = the aim (doctrinal, evangelistic, pastoral, ethical); structure = the arrangement (topical, textual, expository, narrative). They are different axes. A doctrinal purpose is usually carried by a topical structure; an evangelistic purpose may use a narrative structure (a story sermon ending in an appeal); a pastoral purpose may use an expository structure on a comforting psalm. Strong answer keeps the two ideas clearly separate and gives a coherent example.

sa.prompt: Compare doctrinal preaching with pastoral preaching. Where does each begin, and what does each chiefly aim to accomplish?
sa.model: Doctrinal preaching begins with a truth (a belief) and aims to teach it for understanding, acceptance, and changed living; it is typically topical. Pastoral preaching often begins with a problem or need (grief, fear, guilt, a strained marriage) and aims to heal, bringing Scripture to that need as balm and guide. Strong answer notes the different starting points (truth vs. need) and the different aims (teach vs. heal), and may note that both must remain anchored in the Word.

sa.prompt: Explain the urgency that marks evangelistic preaching, using 2 Corinthians 6:2, and show what the example of Felix teaches the evangelist.
sa.model: Strong answer: evangelistic preaching believes a decision is being made every time the gospel is heard, with no neutral ground; 'now is the acceptable time, now is the day of salvation' (2 Cor 6:2) — the call is for today, not someday. Felix trembled under Paul's reasoning of righteousness, temperance, and judgment but postponed his decision to 'a more convenient season' that never came (Acts 24:25). The lesson: the evangelist preaches so that hearers will not make that fatal delay, and ends with a clear, earnest invitation.

sa.prompt: Pastoral preaching can decay into mere secular self-help. Explain this danger and describe how a preacher can keep pastoral preaching genuinely Christian.
sa.model: Strong answer: the peril is that pastoral preaching becomes comfort without Christ — borrowed pop-psychology and advice without the authority of the Word. The world already has counsel enough; what the people of God need is a word from God. The cure: let the sermon meet the real need but heal it with Scripture rather than merely soothe with sentiment; begin with the need but bring the text to bear with its full authority; keep Christ and the gospel, not technique, at the center. Strong answers may cite Paul comforting the grieving with the hope of the resurrection (1 Thess 4:13) rather than with platitudes.

sa.prompt: Using the example of Nathan and David (2 Samuel 12), explain how ethical (prophetic) preaching confronts sin, and what it requires of the preacher.
sa.model: Strong answer: Nathan went to a king guilty of adultery and murder and, by a story that disarmed David's defenses, brought him to self-condemnation and then to the direct word 'Thou art the man' (2 Sam 12:7). Ethical/prophetic preaching names sin plainly, summons to repentance, and marks the road of obedience. It requires of the preacher the willingness to be faithful even when unwelcome — to confront the powerful and to risk the cost. Strong answers may note Nathan's skillful, gracious approach that led to repentance rather than mere rebuke.

sa.prompt: Why must ethical preaching be rooted in grace rather than in moralism? Explain the relationship between law and gospel in a call to righteous living.
sa.model: Strong answer: ethical preaching can curdle into moralism — a list of duties cut off from the gospel — or into bare social scolding. The remedy is to root every command in grace: righteousness is not the way to earn God's favor but the glad response of those who have already received it. Law tells us what to do; only the gospel gives us the heart to do it. The ethical sermon presses obedience, but upon a people first reminded of the mercy that makes obedience possible. Strong answers keep grace prior to and enabling obedience, avoiding both legalism and a gospel with no ethical demand.

sa.prompt: A tragedy has struck your congregation — a sudden death has left the church grieving and fearful. Which purpose of preaching should predominate this Sunday, and how would you preach toward it without abandoning the gospel?
sa.model: Strong answer identifies the therapeutic/pastoral purpose as predominant: the sermon should meet the people in their grief and fear with the comfort and counsel of God's Word. A good plan names the loss honestly, then brings Scripture to bear — Psalm 147:3, Matthew 11:28, or Paul's resurrection hope in 1 Thessalonians 4:13 — comforting with a real word from God rather than sentiment. Strong answers keep Christ central (perhaps an evangelistic note, since death confronts the living with eternity) and avoid both cold doctrine and mere emotional soothing.

sa.prompt: Choose any single Scripture text and show how it could be preached toward at least three of the four purposes (doctrinal, evangelistic, pastoral, ethical). Explain how the aim would shape each sermon.
sa.model: Strong answer takes one text and shows how the SAME passage can serve different aims: e.g., John 3:16 preached doctrinally (the nature of God's love, the meaning of 'only begotten'), evangelistically (a call to 'whosoever' to believe today), pastorally (assurance for a fearful believer that he is loved and shall not perish), and ethically (the love of God as the ground and motive of love for others). The point is that the WiseSpeak method and the text remain the same; the preacher's purpose changes what he draws out and how he applies it. Strong answers tie each treatment clearly to its aim and keep all of them biblical.
